rules.title: Accessibility is the floor
rules.what: Accessibility requirements (keyboard access, focus visibility, semantic structure, labels, contrast, alt text) are never traded away for performance or sobriety.
rules.why: A service some people cannot use serves no need for them at all; excluding users is the largest possible waste. Sobriety that removes access is not sobriety.
rules.how: Follow RGAA/WCAG for the target level: semantic HTML, labelled controls, visible focus, tested keyboard journey. Optimisations must preserve them.

patterns.note: img without alt attribute; candidate only, verify context.

verify.how: Essential journey completed with keyboard only; automated RGAA/WCAG checks run with results recorded.

limits: Automated checks cover a minority of RGAA criteria; observation of real users with assistive tech is the evidence that counts.

rules.title: The lightest medium that carries the information
rules.what: Choose the lightest medium that actually carries the information: text before image, image before video, document before interactive.
rules.why: Media weight is the dominant share of most pages' footprint, and it grows fastest. Matching the medium to the message is the cheapest byte saved.
rules.how: Ask whether a sentence, a table or a static image conveys the same information as the video or animation. If yes, use it.

verify.how: Heavy media items each state what information they carry that a lighter medium could not.

rules.title: Native components rather than reimplemented ones
rules.what: Prefer native components (native select, date picker, details/summary, dialog) over JS reimplementations, unless a measured need overrides.
rules.why: A native component ships zero kilobytes, works on older devices, and stays accessible with the platform's own testing. A JS reimplementation pays for all three again.
rules.how: Try the native element first; justify each replacement (measured requirement the platform cannot meet).

verify.how: Custom widgets have a stated platform gap they close.

limits: Browser support gaps are legitimate; cite them explicitly.

rules.title: Honour reduced-motion preference
rules.what: Animations respect prefers-reduced-motion; large or infinite animations are gated behind it.
rules.why: Motion that some users must block to use the page is a resource spent against accessibility, and often runs continuously on the GPU for no task.
rules.how: Wrap non-essential animation in @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) or disable on the reduced-motion setting.

patterns.note: Keyframe animation defined; verify a prefers-reduced-motion gate exists in the same file.

verify.how: CSS/JS animation code co-located with a reduced-motion media query or equivalent runtime check.

limits: Functional transitions (progress, state change) may be kept short; the gate targets decorative motion.

rules.title: Short and direct journeys
rules.what: Minimise steps and intermediate screens on the user's main tasks; every step is a page load, a request and a chance to abandon.
rules.why: Each unnecessary step costs resources on every completion of the journey, and abandons waste everything spent before them.
rules.how: Map the main journeys, count the steps, remove or merge the ones that gather nothing the user sees or the system needs.

verify.how: Journey step count documented with a reason for each step.

limits: Regulatory or consent steps are not waste; they are marked as such.

rules.title: Errors that save work
rules.what: Validate early, keep user input across steps, and give errors that let the user fix the problem without restarting.
rules.why: A lost form is pure waste: all the resources spent on the abandoned attempt, plus the full cost of doing it again.
rules.how: Client-side validation with server confirmation, field-level errors, preserved input, resumable multi-step processes.

verify.how: A failing submission keeps user input and names the field at fault.

rules.title: Third-party UI on demand
rules.what: Third-party UI elements (maps, chat widgets, video embeds, social embeds) load only on explicit user action or on pages where they serve the task.
rules.why: These embeds are the heaviest items on most pages and often load on every page of the site regardless of use.
rules.how: Static facade (image + click-to-load) for maps and videos, chat widget on action, embeds only on the pages where the task needs them.

patterns.note: Direct embed of heavy third-party UI; verify a click-to-load facade.

verify.how: Embeds are behind a facade or loaded on user action; static fallback present.

rules.title: Show users the impact of their choices
rules.what: Where users choose options with a material resource difference (video quality, sync frequency, storage, AI generation), show the difference plainly and default to the sober option.
rules.why: Users cannot choose sobriety they cannot see; an honest default and a clear choice turn the interface into a lever for lower impact (IT for Green).
rules.how: Default to standard definition or on-demand loading; label heavier options with their measured relative cost; never use guilt or dark patterns.

verify.how: Options with material resource difference are labelled and the default is the sober one.

limits: Displayed figures must come from measurement (see NR-MEASURE-003); otherwise show a relative, qualitative difference.

rules.title: Captions and transcripts for media
rules.what: Provide captions for video with speech, transcripts for audio, and audio description where the image carries information.
rules.why: Media without text alternatives excludes people who are deaf, hard of hearing, blind or in a noisy or silent environment; a transcript also lets everyone skim instead of streaming.
rules.how: <track kind="captions" srclang="fr"> on <video>; a text transcript link next to audio; describe visual-only information.

patterns.note: Video without a track element nearby; captions may be burned in or provided elsewhere.

verify.how: Each media item with speech has captions or a transcript; checked against RGAA theme 4 / WCAG 1.2.

rules.title: Never block zoom
rules.what: Let users zoom and resize text: no user-scalable=no or maximum-scale=1 in the viewport, and layouts that reflow at 200% and 400%.
rules.why: Blocking zoom excludes people with low vision, who then cannot read the page at all.
rules.how: <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">; relative units; test at 200% text size and 320px width.

verify.how: Page usable at 200% zoom and 320 CSS px width (RGAA 10.4, 10.11 / WCAG 1.4.4, 1.4.10).

rules.title: Visible keyboard focus
rules.what: Keep a visible focus indicator on every interactive element; never remove outlines without a replacement.
rules.why: Without a visible focus, people who navigate by keyboard or switch devices cannot tell where they are.
rules.how: :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid currentColor; outline-offset: 2px; } instead of outline: none.

patterns.note: Outline removed; check a :focus-visible replacement exists.

verify.how: Keyboard-only walk of the journey shows focus at every step (RGAA 10.7 / WCAG 2.4.7).

rules.title: Plain language
rules.what: Write interface text and content in plain language: short sentences, common words, one idea per sentence, explained jargon.
rules.why: Complex wording excludes people with cognitive disabilities, low literacy or a different first language, and makes everyone take longer and make more errors.
rules.how: Front-load the key information; explain terms on first use; offer an easy-to-read (FALC) version for essential public information.

verify.how: Essential texts reviewed against plain-language guidelines (WCAG 3.1.5, FALC).

origin: FALC (facile à lire et à comprendre)
